title: Flexible reserved slots: timeboxed leasing, hot-rebalance, and progressive eviction PRD
creator: Sana Gupta
description: Problem: Customers with reserved capacity want stronger utilization guarantees without sacrificing predictability. Current dedicated reservations are coarse: either fully reserved pools or soft-burst behavior. We see two recurring requests: (1) customers want timeboxed leases (short-term guaranteed slots for scheduled jobs or critical windows), and (2) operators want safe reclaiming/rebalancing of idle reserved slots to improve utilization. This PRD proposes 'Flexible Reserved Slots' — a leasing model that lets tenants obtain short-duration guaranteed capacity, plus a hot-rebalance mechanism to temporarily repurpose idle slots across tenants with progressive eviction and clear SLAs.
background: Existing reserved pools provide long-lived guarantees but lead to underutilization in predictable patterns (night/weekends, batch windows). Various internal PRDs have proposed predictive buffering and ephemeral bridging, but customers also requested explicit timeboxing and auditable slot handoffs. We must balance tenant isolation guarantees, billing clarity, and SLO compliance. This feature will sit on top of the existing capacity allocator and routing policies and integrate with chargeback and observability surfaces in Console.
goals: Allow tenants to request short-term leased reserved slots (timeboxed reservations) with clear start/end and pricing
Enable cluster-level hot-rebalance to mark idle leased slots as reclaimable and temporarily route other tenants' bursts into them without violating committed leases (progressive eviction on reclaim)
Provide predictable eviction semantics and telemetry for both lessor and borrower tenants
Surface lease lifecycle and costs in Console, with audit logs for compliance
non_goals: Replace long-term reserved capacity contracts or SLA tiers
Automate cross-account transfers of long-lived reservations
Change model-level runtime kernels or per-model quantization profiles
user_stories: As an SRE for AcmeCorp, I want to reserve 4 slots for a 6-hour nightly ingest window so that my jobs complete predictably
As a platform operator, I want to reclaim idle leased slots when utilization falls below threshold and lend them for ephemeral bursts across tenants with clear rollback rules
As a finance lead, I need invoice-level breakdowns showing timeboxed lease charges and any reclaimed/borrowed usage
acceptance_criteria: API: createLease(start_time, end_time, slot_count, priority, fallback_policy) returns lease_id and validation with conflict errors
Scheduler: leased slots are tracked with lease_id in allocator and honored for route decisions between start_time and end_time
Hot-rebalance: operator-configurable idle threshold and reclaim window will mark leased slots as reclaimable and allow temporary routing of non-guaranteed traffic
Eviction semantics: borrower workload can be preempted with a 60s grace period (configurable 30-300s) and a progressive crediting mechanism applied to borrower billing on preemption
Console: lease lifecycle (requested/active/reclaimed/evicted/closed) visible per-tenant and per-slot with timestamps and audit log entries
Billing: charges are split into 'lease fee' (timeboxed reservation) and 'borrowed usage' with clear unit pricing on invoice
Telemetry: new metrics exposed (lease_active_count, lease_reclaimed_count, lease_evictions, lease_prestige_latency_delta) and traces annotated with lease_id
Security/Audit: every reclaim and handoff generates an immutable audit record (who, when, why, decision) stored per-account
success_metrics: Increase cluster reserved-slot utilization by 12% in pilot clusters within 6 weeks
Reduce unbillable idle reserved-hours by 25% for participating customers within quarter
Customer satisfaction: 80% of pilot tenants report predictable completion for scheduled windows
Mean time to preemption notification <= 60s and error spike due to preemptions < 0.5% of calls
rolling_out_plan: Phase 0: Design + API spec and internal scheduler spike (2 sprints). Phase 1: Pilot with three enterprise tenants and a single zone; enable hot-rebalance as opt-in. Phase 2: Rollout to all dedicated clusters with default opt-out reclaiming. Phase 3: Console billing and audit retention expansion. Each phase gated by SLO/regression tests and customer signoff.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Add lease instrumentations to runtime request headers and token accounting. Build Grafana/Console dashboards showing lease occupancy, reclaim events, eviction counts, and tenant-level cost impact. Alerts for reclaim rates exceeding threshold or preemption-caused error spikes.
technical_considerations: Allocator changes: add lease table keyed by lease_id and time window; efficient range queries for active leases during routing
Routing: leases should be first-class routing constraints: route to nodes with matching free leased slots before falling back
KV cache impact: reclaimed slots may have warm KV caches required by borrower workloads; consider cold-start penalty SLOs
Billing & Quota: billing pipeline must accept lease metadata and attribute slot-hours to lease fee bucket
Consistency: implement best-effort lease enforcement; strong enforcement requires tight coupling with autoscaler and node-level guards
Data retention: audit logs for reclaims must be retained per compliance policy (configurable retention)
ux_notes: Console Add Lease wizard: pick start/end, slot count, target zone(s), fallback (soft-burst, degrade-to-hosted, queue), and a preview of estimated cost. Lease timeline view in tenant dashboard showing active and upcoming leases, reclaim events, and impacted requests with links to trace.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive hot-rebalance could violate perceived guarantees -> Mitigation: require tenant opt-in to make their leases reclaimable or enable only when lease has been idle for a conservative window
Risk: billing complexity/confusion -> Mitigation: include cost preview at purchase and line-item invoice breakdowns; initial pilot includes finance walkthrough
Risk: preemption leads to increased errors for borrower tenants -> Mitigation: progressive eviction with notice signal (60s) and crediting mechanism; recommended borrower settings to checkpoint work
Risk: audit/compliance objections for cross-tenant re-use -> Mitigation: full audit trail with reason codes and option to disable cross-tenant borrowing for regulated customers
open_questions: Q1: Default grace period for eviction (30s/60s/120s)? Current proposed default=60s
Q2: Pricing model: flat per-slot-hour vs discount for reclaimed hours? Need finance input
Q3: Should reclaimed slots require tenant consent at purchase (opt-in reclaimable) or be opt-out?
Q4: How do we present lease precedence vs long-term reservation? Precedence hierarchy needed
security_and_compliance: No cryptographic secrets changes. Audit log retention must support enterprise retention controls. Ensure lease audit integrates with KMS audit where required. Security review flagged for special regulated customers - not required for pilot but required for GA customers in regulated industries.
implementation_notes: Backend: allocator + billing + routing change. Runtime: annotate calls with lease_id to enable traceability. Console: new UI components and billing preview. Telemetry: update ingestion schema to accept lease-tagged usage records.
acceptance_test_plan: End-to-end test that creates a lease, routes guaranteed traffic, marks lease idle and triggers reclaim window, verifies borrower requests succeed, issues eviction and validates grace period behavior, and verifies billing attribution and audit log creation. Automation in CI and nightly stress tests.
